scenarios.title: A negative scan: a scan that cannot say no

evidence: Scenario negative-scan-a-scan-that-cannot-say-no carries stable content version 0.1.0.
Capability version 0.1.0-alpha.48 is bound by this audit.
The declarative scenario schema validates a bounded fictional patient profile.
This scenario declares 7 objectives; the contract allows at most 5.
negative-scan-fixtures.ts binds seed 6841 and content 0.1.0 to expert, incomplete-care, recovery, and no-action contrasts. No leak, perfusion, or healing model is claimed.

negative-scan.ts runs two authored transitions. At 45 minutes the observations are repeated unchanged, he has vomited once, and he has still passed no flatus, so the only thing that has moved is how long this has been true. The operating team answers 60 minutes after it is contacted, confirms the procedure, the anastomosis and the findings from its own record, states that a report of no evidence of a leak is not the same as no leak, and takes ownership of re-imaging, direct assessment, and any return to theatre. Nothing arrives uncontacted, because the failure being taught is a ward re-reading a report instead of ringing the surgeons. The patient deliberately never deteriorates: a crash would make the decision for the learner.

The learner records the operation and the course it predicts, records the failure to progress against that course with its duration, records what the reported scan does and does not exclude, contacts the operating team, records bounded qualified-team surgical intent, and reviews the boundaries. Excluding a leak because the scan was negative, dismissing the observations as routine after bowel surgery, repeating the scan tomorrow, and treating the numbers overnight are each refused, and the refusal of the dismissal accepts its premise while rejecting the inference.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The recorded operative course, the recorded failure to progress, the recorded limits of the scan, contact with the operating team, bounded surgical intent, the boundary review, and a current full assessment permit handoff with the diagnosis and the operative decision open. Instructor takeover bounds a run with no escalation at 180 minutes, or an unfinished session at eight hours.

Observed-state guidance and learner-paused example 0.1.0 use ordinary recorded actions. Unassisted mode is silent and coached withholds the two non-urgent beats. The prompts read only the learner’s own recorded steps and never say whether this is a leak, because that is what the lesson deliberately leaves open and what neither the observation nor the scan can settle. The example is driven through the real engine in tests rather than asserted as a script, and it ends with the leak neither confirmed nor excluded: an example that arrived at a diagnosis would teach the reflex this lesson exists to refuse. Both authored waits are narrated as contrasts rather than as clinical waiting, since the escalation has already been made by then.

Seven event-bound objectives distinguish reading a patient against the course his own operation predicts, a trajectory from a single reading, a report of no evidence from an exclusion, returning the patient to the team that made the anastomosis, bounded qualified-team intent, what two small single-centre literatures pointing opposite ways each license, and accountable handoff. Refused shortcuts remain visible, and no leak, operative decision, or outcome is certified.

rising-requirement.ts runs two authored transitions. At 10 minutes, while the learner is still waiting for the team, he asks a fourth time and passive extension stops him mid-sentence, while the pulse, capillary refill, sensation and every monitored observation stay exactly as they were, so the only thing that moves is the requirement and the clock. The surgical team answers 20 minutes after it is called — sooner than this module’s first lesson, because what is escalated is time-critical rather than uncertain — confirms the fracture and its timing from its own record, states that a single reading neither establishes nor excludes this, and takes ownership of repeat assessment, further measurement, and the decision to decompress. Nothing arrives uncalled.

The learner records the injury with its elapsed hours, records the rising requirement as a trajectory, records what one pressure reading cannot decide, calls the team that owns the decision, records bounded qualified-team intent, and reviews the boundaries. Reasoning from a present pulse to an intact compartment, excluding on a remembered cut-off, increasing the analgesia and reviewing in the morning, and waiting for a repeat pressure before calling are each refused, and the analgesia refusal objects to the deferral rather than to comfort.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The recorded injury and clock, the recorded requirement, the recorded limits of the reading, the call to the surgical team, bounded decompression intent, the boundary review, and a current full assessment permit handoff with the diagnosis and the operative decision open. Instructor takeover bounds a run with no escalation at 90 minutes — half this module’s first lesson, because here the harm is the delay — or an unfinished session at eight hours.

Observed-state guidance and learner-paused example 0.1.0 use ordinary recorded actions. Unassisted mode is silent and coached withholds the two non-urgent beats. The prompts read only the learner’s own recorded steps and never say whether this is compartment syndrome, because no measure available in the lesson can settle that. The example is driven through the real engine in tests rather than asserted as a script, and it calls the team before any further number is sought, because the interval spent obtaining one is the harm being taught.

Eight event-bound objectives distinguish carrying the clock on a limb, reading a requirement as a finding, refusing an artery as evidence about a compartment, refusing one reading as the discriminating quantity, calling before the number, bounded qualified-team intent, two measures that fail in opposite directions, and accountable handoff. scenarios.title: An unfinished survey: a patient who cannot be asked

evidence: Scenario unfinished-survey-a-patient-who-cannot-be-asked carries stable content version 0.1.0.
Capability version 0.1.0-alpha.48 is bound by this audit.
The declarative scenario schema validates a bounded fictional patient profile.
This scenario declares 8 objectives; the contract allows at most 5.
unfinished-survey-fixtures.ts binds seed 5137 and content 0.1.0 to expert, incomplete-care, recovery, and no-action contrasts. No injury, healing, sedation, or neurological model is claimed.

unfinished-survey.ts runs two authored transitions. At 10 minutes sedation is lightened for the routine neurological assessment and he localises to the right, does not move the left arm, and grimaces when the left forearm is handled, while the ventilator, drain, pressures and every monitored number stay exactly as they were and the ward asks a second time about the bed — so the only thing that changes is how much of him can be examined. The trauma team answers 25 minutes after it is asked — longer than this module’s second lesson, because what is requested is a deliberate reassessment rather than a time-critical decision — confirms from its own record that no tertiary survey has been documented, states that the secondary survey entry records an examination rather than an absence of injury, and takes ownership of completing the survey, re-reviewing the imaging against it, and anything that follows. Nothing arrives uncalled.

The learner records why the examination behind the record was limited, records what the injury list rests on, records that no tertiary survey has been performed or documented, asks the team that owns the survey to complete it, records bounded qualified-team intent, and reviews the boundaries. Treating the documented secondary survey as the assessment, leaning on the whole-body imaging to exclude the rest, reading his silence as reassurance, and clearing him now to review if something appears are each refused, and the clearing refusal objects to recording him as fully assessed rather than to the step-down itself.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The recorded examination limits, the recorded basis of the injury list, the recorded absence of a tertiary survey, the request to the trauma team, bounded survey intent, the boundary review, and a current full assessment permit handoff with the survey and any missed injury open. Instructor takeover bounds a run with no escalation at 180 minutes — this module’s first lesson’s interval rather than its second’s, because here the harm is not measured minute to minute — or an unfinished session at twelve hours.

Observed-state guidance and learner-paused example 0.1.0 use ordinary recorded actions. Unassisted mode is silent and coached withholds the two non-urgent beats. The prompts read only the learner’s own recorded steps and never assert that a missed injury exists, because nothing available in the lesson can establish that and asserting it would remove the difficulty the lesson is about. The example is driven through the real engine in tests rather than asserted as a script, and it asks for the survey while the patient is still sedated and there is nothing to show, because an example that waited for the sedation window would teach that the finding is what justifies the position.

Eight event-bound objectives distinguish recording what a patient could contribute to his own examination, reading an injury list as a record of findings rather than an exclusion, refusing a complete record of a limited examination as an assessment, recording an unfinished survey as a live finding, asking the team that owns the step to take it, bounded qualified-team intent, a step worth taking whose evidence does not show it works, and accountable handoff of an assessment recorded as unfinished. Refused shortcuts remain visible, and no missed injury, disposition, or outcome is certified.
